feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Evidence: iteration 0 and 4 (wheel_track 0.12 m, five sensors, kp 4.0, mass 0.6 kg) scored 96.84, with s-bend max_error 0.0703 m, line loss 2 per run, and steering_oscillation 0.2533. Oval and slalom max_error were about 0.062 m. Iteration 2 (wheel_track 0.14 m, mass 0.5 kg, kp 7.0) fell to 74.95, but it changed kp and mass as well as track width, so that drop cannot be attributed to track width alone. Iteration 3 changed footprint, row and drivetrain together and scored 48.12. Turn rate is wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so narrowing the track raises yaw per unit of command by about 1.2 times. Your 0.10 m candidate therefore tests more turn authority, and it also raises the oscillation risk. Next race: if s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.25, the cause is probably the higher effective gain, so I will lower kp in the controller rather than change the geometry again. If steering_oscillation stays below about 0.25 and s-bend max_error is still above 0.06 m with line loss at 2, propose wheel_track 0.08 m as the next step. If the score falls below 96.84, revert wheel_track to 0.12 m.
requested_changes: If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 at wheel_track 0.10 m: keep the geometry and tell me, so I can lower kp from 4.0 toward 3.5 to restore the iteration 0 yaw response per command (iteration 0 oscillation 0.2533 at kp 4.0 is already at the limit).

If s-bend max_error stays above 0.06 m with line loss at 2 and steering_oscillation below about 0.25: propose wheel_track 0.08 m, citing iteration 0's max_error of 0.0703 m and the contract yaw relation.
If the score falls below 96.84 at wheel_track 0.10 m: revert wheel_track to 0.12 m, citing iteration 2's drop to 74.95 as a warning that turn-authority changes can cost score when oscillation rises.
